questions.text: A trader purchased goods marked ₦800,000 subject to a trade discount of 15%. What amount should be entered in the purchases account
questions.explanation: ₦800,000 × 85% = ₦680,000. Trade discount is deducted before recording the purchase.

questions.text: A machine was purchased for ₦4,000,000. Transportation cost was ₦120,000 and installation cost was ₦180,000. The initial cost of the machine is
A business has assets of ₦8,500,000 and liabilities of ₦2,700,000. Its capital is
questions.explanation: Capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₦8.5m − ₦2.7m = ₦5.8m.

questions.text: The owner introduced ₦500,000 additional capital and withdrew ₦200,000 during the year. If opening capital was ₦4,000,000 and closing capital was ₦4,600,000, the profit was
questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦4.6m + ₦200k − ₦500k − ₦4m = ₦300,000.

questions.text: A purchase of office equipment was recorded in the purchases account. This is an error of
questions.explanation: Equipment is a non-current asset, not goods purchased for resale. The error is one of principle.

questions.text: A credit sale of ₦65,000 was recorded as ₦56,000 in both the sales and customer's account. This is an error of
questions.explanation: The wrong amount was entered in both accounts. This is an error of original entry.

questions.text: A transaction of ₦90,000 was completely omitted from the books. The trial balance will
questions.explanation: Both debit and credit entries are omitted, so the trial balance remains balanced.

questions.text: A payment of ₦45,000 to a creditor was credited to the bank account but omitted from the creditor's account. The trial balance will show
questions.explanation: The credit entry exists without its corresponding debit. Therefore credits exceed debits by ₦45,000.

questions.text: A debtor owing ₦250,000 was allowed a cash discount of 4%. The amount received was
A supplier's account shows ₦600,000. Goods worth ₦80,000 are returned and a 5% discount is received on the balance. Amount paid is
A three-column cash book has cash ₦150,000 and bank ₦500,000. A cheque of ₦90,000 is withdrawn from the bank and placed in the cash till. The new balances are
questions.explanation: Cash increases by ₦90,000 while bank decreases by ₦90,000. Cash = ₦240,000; Bank = ₦410,000.

questions.text: A cheque received from a customer is dishonoured. The customer's account should be
questions.explanation: The original receipt is cancelled, so the customer's debt is restored by debiting the customer's account.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to be discovered first from a bank statement rather than from the business's own records
questions.explanation: Bank charges are normally first seen on the bank statement and then entered in the cash book.

questions.text: The bank statement shows an overdraft of ₦400,000. Unpresented cheques amount to ₦70,000 while uncredited lodgements amount to ₦100,000. The cash-book overdraft is
A standing order appearing on the bank statement but absent from the cash book should be entered by
questions.explanation: A standing order is a payment made through the bank, reducing the bank balance. The bank column is therefore credited.

questions.text: A direct lodgement of ₦120,000 appears on the bank statement but has not been entered in the cash book. The cash book should be
questions.explanation: The direct lodgement increases the bank balance, so the bank column is debited.

questions.text: A business's closing inventory is ₦900,000. Included in the figure are goods held on behalf of another business worth ₦100,000. The correct closing inventory is
questions.explanation: Goods belonging to another business are excluded. ₦900,000 − ₦100,000 = ₦800,000.

questions.text: Goods sent to an agent on consignment but unsold at year-end should be
options: included in the consignor's closing inventory
questions.explanation: Ownership remains with the consignor until the goods are sold.

questions.text: Opening inventory is ₦600,000, purchases ₦3,200,000, carriage inward ₦200,000 and closing inventory ₦700,000. Cost of sales is
Sales are ₦5,000,000 and gross profit is 30% of sales. Cost of sales is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 30% × ₦5m = ₦1.5m. Cost of sales = ₦5m − ₦1.5m = ₦3.5m.

questions.text: A trader marks goods up by 25% on cost. If the selling price is ₦750,000, the cost price is
questions.explanation: Selling price = 125% of cost. Cost = ₦750,000 ÷ 1.25 = ₦600,000.

questions.text: A trader makes a profit of 20% on cost. If the cost of goods is ₦450,000, the selling price is
A trader sells goods at a margin of 25%. If sales are ₦2,400,000, the cost of sales is
Which of the following would increase gross profit, all other things remaining equal
questions.explanation: Closing inventory is deducted from cost of sales. A higher closing inventory therefore reduces cost of sales and increases gross profit.

questions.text: Opening inventory was overstated by ₦50,000 while closing inventory was correctly stated. The reported gross profit would be
questions.explanation: Overstated opening inventory causes cost of sales to be overstated, so gross profit is understated by ₦50,000.

questions.text: Gross profit is ₦1,500,000. Operating expenses are ₦800,000 and commission income is ₦120,000. Net profit is
Rent paid during the year was ₦600,000. This includes ₦80,000 prepaid for next year. At year-end, rent owing is ₦50,000. The rent expense for the year is
questions.explanation: Expense = Cash paid − Prepayment + Accrual. ₦600,000 − ₦80,000 + ₦50,000 = ₦570,000.

questions.text: An accrued expense is shown in the statement of financial position as
questions.explanation: An accrued expense is an amount owed and is therefore a liability.

questions.text: A prepaid expense is
questions.explanation: It represents a future economic benefit already paid for, so it is an asset.

questions.text: A business receives ₦900,000 for services, of which ₦150,000 relates to the following accounting period. Current-period income is
A machine costs ₦5,000,000, has a residual value of ₦500,000 and a useful life of 9 years. Annual straight-line depreciation is
An asset costing ₦2,000,000 is depreciated at 10% per annum using the reducing-balance method. Its carrying amount after two years is
An asset cost ₦1,500,000 and has accumulated depreciation of ₦900,000. It is sold for ₦520,000. The result is
Which depreciation method normally produces equal depreciation charges each year
questions.explanation: Straight-line depreciation allocates the depreciable amount equally over the useful life.

questions.text: The main purpose of depreciation is to
options: allocate the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life
increase the market value of assets
questions.explanation: Depreciation is an accounting allocation, not a cash reserve.

questions.text: A machine has a cost of ₦3,000,000 and accumulated depreciation of ₦1,200,000. Its carrying amount is
Which of the following is revenue expenditure
questions.explanation: Routine repairs maintain an existing asset and are therefore revenue expenditure.

questions.text: Expenditure incurred to substantially improve the capacity of an existing machine is generally
questions.explanation: It provides an additional future economic benefit and is therefore capital in nature.

questions.text: A debtor owing ₦200,000 is expected to pay only 70% of the debt. The irrecoverable portion is
questions.explanation: Expected recovery = 70%. Irrecoverable = 30% × ₦200,000 = ₦60,000.

questions.text: Trade receivables are ₦1,200,000 and an allowance of 5% is required. Net receivables are
questions.explanation: Allowance = 5% × ₦1.2m = ₦60,000. Net receivables = ₦1.14m.

questions.text: An existing allowance for doubtful debts is ₦50,000. The new required allowance is ₦70,000. The increase of ₦20,000 will
questions.explanation: An increase in the allowance is recognized as an expense, reducing profit.

questions.text: A customer owing ₦150,000 pays ₦144,000 in full settlement. The discount allowed is
A supplier is owed ₦400,000 and grants a discount of ₦20,000 for prompt settlement. The cash payment is
When a discount is allowed to a customer, the customer's personal account is
questions.explanation: The discount reduces the customer's debt, so the customer's account is credited.

questions.text: When a business receives a discount from a supplier, the discount received account is normally
questions.explanation: Discount received is an income/gain and is therefore credited.

questions.text: Current assets are ₦6,000,000 and current liabilities are ₦2,000,000. The current ratio is
Current assets are ₦5,000,000, inventory is ₦2,000,000 and current liabilities are ₦1,500,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦5m − ₦2m = ₦3m. ₦3m ÷ ₦1.5m = 2:1.

questions.text: A business with a current ratio of 3:1 pays a current liability from cash. The current ratio will generally
questions.explanation: Both current assets and current liabilities decrease, but because the original ratio is above 1:1, the ratio increases.

questions.text: Gross profit is ₦1,800,000 and sales are ₦6,000,000. Gross profit margin is
Net profit is ₦600,000 and sales are ₦4,000,000. Net profit margin is
Cost of sales is ₦6,000,000 and average inventory is ₦1,000,000. Inventory turnover is
questions.explanation: ₦6m ÷ ₦1m = 6 times.

questions.text: A fall in inventory turnover may indicate
questions.explanation: A lower turnover generally indicates that inventory is being sold more slowly.

questions.text: Credit sales are ₦5,400,000 and average receivables are ₦900,000. Receivables turnover is
If receivables turnover is 9 times, the approximate collection period using a 360-day year is
Capital employed is ₦8,000,000 and operating profit is ₦1,200,000. ROCE is
A company has long-term debt of ₦3,000,000 and equity of ₦6,000,000. The debt-to-equity ratio is
A high gearing ratio generally means that a company
questions.explanation: High gearing indicates a relatively high dependence on long-term borrowed funds.

questions.text: Direct materials are ₦1,500,000, direct labour ₦900,000 and factory overhead ₦600,000. Opening WIP is ₦250,000 and closing WIP is ₦350,000. Cost of production is
Which of the following is an indirect material
options: Flour used in a particular batch of bread
Timber used for a specific table
Lubricating oil used generally in a factory
Leather used for a specific pair of shoes
questions.explanation: General factory lubricating oil cannot conveniently be traced to a specific unit of output, so it is indirect material.

questions.text: Factory electricity is generally classified as
questions.explanation: Factory electricity is an indirect production cost.

questions.text: Partners A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. If the divisible profit is ₦2,000,000, B's share is
A and B share profits 5:3. If the total profit is ₦1,600,000, A receives

A partnership has profits of ₦1,500,000. Partner A receives a salary of ₦200,000 and interest on capital of ₦100,000. The remaining profit is shared between A and B in the ratio 3:2. B's total share is
questions.explanation: Residual profit = ₦1.5m − ₦200k − ₦100k = ₦1.2m. B receives 2/5 × ₦1.2m = ₦480,000.

questions.text: Goodwill in a partnership mainly represents
options: the value of the firm's reputation and other advantages
questions.explanation: Goodwill reflects intangible advantages such as reputation and customer loyalty.

questions.text: When a new partner is admitted, goodwill is often adjusted because
options: the old partners surrender part of their existing interest in the firm's goodwill
questions.explanation: The incoming partner acquires an interest in the existing business, including its goodwill.

questions.text: On dissolution of a partnership, the realization account is prepared mainly to determine
questions.explanation: It records disposal of assets and settlement of liabilities to determine the realization profit or loss.

questions.text: A partner takes over an asset valued at ₦300,000 during dissolution. The partner's capital/current account will generally be
questions.explanation: The partner is taking the asset personally, so the amount is debited to the partner's account.

questions.text: A company is authorized to issue 2,000,000 shares but has issued 1,400,000. The number of unissued shares is
A company issues 500,000 ₦2 shares at ₦2.80 each. The share premium is
Which statement about ordinary shares is correct
options: They always carry a fixed dividend
They represent ownership interest in the company
They must be repaid on a fixed date
questions.explanation: Ordinary shareholders are owners of the company.

questions.text: A company has 800,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each and declares a dividend of 15%. The dividend declared is
Debenture interest is generally treated as
questions.explanation: Debenture holders are creditors, so interest is a finance expense.

questions.text: The main difference between a debenture holder and an ordinary shareholder is that the debenture holder is
questions.explanation: Debenture holders lend money to the company and are therefore creditors.

questions.text: A non-profit organization receives subscriptions of ₦1,200,000. Opening arrears are ₦80,000, closing arrears ₦120,000, opening subscriptions received in advance ₦50,000 and closing advance ₦70,000. Subscription income is
The accumulated fund of a non-profit organization is increased by
questions.explanation: A surplus increases the organization's net assets/accumulated fund.

questions.text: A receipts and payments account records
options: all cash and bank receipts and payments
questions.explanation: It records all cash/bank movements, whether capital or revenue.

questions.text: Opening capital is ₦2,500,000, closing capital is ₦3,200,000, drawings are ₦400,000 and additional capital is ₦300,000. Profit is
A trader's capital increased from ₦3,000,000 to ₦4,000,000. During the year, drawings were ₦600,000 and additional capital was ₦250,000. Profit was
Opening trade receivables are ₦800,000. Credit sales are ₦3,500,000. Cash received from customers is ₦2,600,000, returns inward are ₦100,000 and discounts allowed are ₦50,000. Closing receivables are
The purchases ledger control account represents the total amount owed to
questions.explanation: The purchases ledger control account summarizes trade payables.

questions.text: Which of the following errors will NOT affect the agreement of a trial balance
options: Posting only one side of a transaction
Incorrect addition of one side of an account
Posting a debit as a credit
questions.explanation: Complete omission means neither side is recorded, so both totals remain affected equally.

questions.text: A transaction of ₦25,000 was debited to an account but the corresponding credit was omitted. The suspense account should be
questions.explanation: A missing credit means debits exceed credits. To correct the imbalance, the suspense account receives a credit of ₦25,000.

questions.text: A suspense account has a debit balance of ₦40,000. This indicates that
questions.explanation: A debit balance means debits exceed credits by that amount.

questions.text: An error in which an amount is posted to the wrong account of the same class is usually classified as
questions.explanation: Posting to the wrong account while maintaining the correct general classification is an error of commission.

questions.text: The accounting concept that requires similar accounting methods to be used consistently from one period to another is
questions.explanation: The consistency concept promotes comparability between accounting periods.

questions.text: The business entity concept assumes that
options: the owner and business are the same accounting entity
the business is separate from its owner
liabilities belong to the owner personally
questions.explanation: The business is treated as a separate entity from its owner.

questions.text: The going-concern concept assumes that
options: the business will continue operating for the foreseeable future
all assets must be sold immediately
questions.explanation: Going concern assumes continued operation.

questions.text: A business purchases equipment for ₦1,000,000, paying ₦400,000 cash and owing ₦600,000. The immediate effect is
options: assets increase by ₦1,000,000 and liabilities increase by ₦600,000
assets increase by ₦600,000 and liabilities increase by ₦400,000
questions.explanation: Equipment increases by ₦1m, cash decreases ₦400k, giving a net asset increase of ₦600k, while the payable increases liabilities by ₦600k.

questions.text: Assets increase by ₦700,000 while liabilities increase by ₦200,000. The effect on capital is
questions.explanation: Since Assets = Capital + Liabilities: Increase in capital = ₦700k − ₦200k = ₦500,000.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦6,000,000 and current liabilities of ₦2,000,000. It purchases inventory worth ₦500,000 on credit. The new current ratio is
questions.explanation: New current assets = ₦6.5m. New current liabilities = ₦2.5m. ₦6.5m ÷ ₦2.5m = 2.6:1.

questions.text: Current assets are ₦4,000,000 and current liabilities are ₦2,000,000. A current liability of ₦400,000 is paid in cash. The new current ratio is
questions.explanation: New current assets = ₦3.6m. New current liabilities = ₦1.6m. ₦3.6m ÷ ₦1.6m = 2.25:1.

questions.text: Inventory is excluded from the acid-test ratio mainly because
options: it may take time to convert into cash
questions.explanation: Inventory is less liquid because it normally has to be sold before becoming cash.

questions.text: Sales are ₦10,000,000, gross profit is ₦3,500,000 and operating expenses are ₦2,000,000. Operating profit margin is
If gross profit margin rises while selling prices remain unchanged, one likely explanation is that
options: cost of sales has fallen relative to sales
questions.explanation: Gross profit margin rises when the difference between sales and cost of sales becomes proportionally larger.

questions.text: Credit purchases are ₦4,800,000 and average trade payables are ₦800,000. Payables turnover is
A fall in the payables turnover ratio generally indicates that the business is
questions.explanation: Lower turnover generally means suppliers' debts are being settled less frequently/slower.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an objective of accounting
questions.explanation: Accounting provides information; it cannot guarantee profitability.

questions.text: The main purpose of public sector accounting is to
questions.explanation: Public sector accounting emphasizes accountability, control and stewardship of public funds.

questions.text: A government department receives ₦15,000,000 specifically for constructing a public school. The expenditure is primarily
questions.explanation: Construction of a long-term public asset is capital expenditure.

questions.text: A business reports a profit of ₦1,500,000. Depreciation is ₦250,000. Trade receivables increase by ₦300,000 while trade payables increase by ₦150,000. Using the simplified indirect method, cash generated from operations before other adjustments is
questions.explanation: Start with profit: ₦1,500,000. Add depreciation: +₦250,000. Less increase in receivables: −₦300,000. Add increase in payables: +₦150,000. = ₦1,500,000 + ₦250,000 − ₦300,000 + ₦150,000 = ₦1,600,000.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the accounting equation
questions.explanation: The fundamental accounting equation is Assets = Capital + Liabilities.

questions.text: A proprietor introduced a motor vehicle valued at ₦4,000,000 into the business. The immediate effect is to
questions.explanation: The business receives an asset, while the owner's interest in the business increases by the same amount.

questions.text: A business purchased furniture for ₦600,000 on credit. Which accounts are affected
questions.explanation: Furniture is debited because it increases, while the creditor is credited because the business now owes the supplier.

questions.text: The owner withdrew ₦150,000 cash for personal use. The correct entries are
questions.explanation: Drawings are debited because they reduce owner's equity, while cash is credited because cash leaves the business.

questions.text: Which transaction affects only the composition of assets
questions.explanation: Cash decreases while inventory increases by the same amount.

questions.text: A business purchased goods worth ₦900,000 less 10% trade discount. The amount recorded in purchases is
Which of the following is deducted from invoice price before recording purchases
questions.explanation: Trade discount is deducted from the listed price before the transaction is recorded.

questions.text: A trader bought goods for ₦500,000 and paid carriage inward of ₦40,000. The total cost of the goods is
questions.explanation: Carriage inward is part of the cost of bringing goods into the business: ₦500,000 + ₦40,000 = ₦540,000.

questions.text: Carriage outward is normally treated as
questions.explanation: Carriage outward relates to delivering goods to customers and is therefore a selling/distribution expense.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital expenditure
questions.explanation: A delivery van provides benefits over several accounting periods and is therefore a non-current asset.

questions.text: A machine costing ₦2,400,000 has an estimated residual value of ₦240,000 and a useful life of 6 years. Annual straight-line depreciation is
An asset costing ₦3,000,000 is depreciated at 20% reducing balance. Its carrying amount after two years is
An asset has a carrying amount of ₦700,000 and is sold for ₦850,000. The business makes a
Depreciation is best described as
options: the creation of cash for asset replacement
the fall in market price of an asset only
systematic allocation of an asset's depreciable amount
questions.explanation: Depreciation allocates the depreciable cost of a non-current asset over its useful life.

questions.text: Which concept requires expenses to be recognized in the period in which the related revenue is recognized
questions.explanation: The matching principle associates expenses with the revenue they helped generate.

questions.text: The prudence concept requires accountants to
questions.explanation: Prudence requires reasonable caution so that assets/income are not overstated and liabilities/expenses are not understated.

questions.text: The concept that assumes a business will continue operating is
questions.explanation: The going-concern assumption means the business is expected to continue operating for the foreseeable future.

questions.text: A business owner uses ₦100,000 of business cash to pay his personal school fees. This should be recorded as
questions.explanation: Personal withdrawals by the owner are drawings, not business expenses.

questions.text: A transaction completely omitted from the books is an
questions.explanation: Complete failure to record a transaction is an error of omission.

questions.text: A purchase of furniture is recorded in the purchases account. This is
questions.explanation: Furniture is a non-current asset, so treating it as purchases violates the appropriate classification.

questions.text: A credit purchase of ₦75,000 is recorded as ₦57,000 in both the purchases and supplier's accounts. This is
questions.explanation: The transaction was recorded in the correct accounts but with the wrong amount.

questions.text: A transaction is completely omitted from the books. The trial balance will
questions.explanation: Neither the debit nor credit side has been recorded, so the two sides remain equal.

questions.text: A payment of ₦30,000 was debited to the creditor's account but the bank account was not credited. The trial balance will show
questions.explanation: A debit has been entered without the corresponding credit, producing a debit excess of ₦30,000.

questions.text: The main purpose of a suspense account is to
options: temporarily hold unexplained trial balance differences
questions.explanation: A suspense account temporarily accommodates an unexplained difference until errors are located and corrected.

questions.text: Which error is most likely to be detected by a trial balance
questions.explanation: A missing corresponding credit causes the trial balance totals to disagree.

questions.text: A bank statement shows a favourable balance of ₦850,000. Unpresented cheques are ₦120,000 and uncredited lodgements are ₦70,000. Assuming no other differences, the cash-book balance is
questions.explanation: Cash-book balance = bank statement balance − unpresented cheques + uncredited lodgements = ₦850,000 − ₦120,000 + ₦70,000 = ₦800,000.

questions.text: A cheque received from a customer and entered in the cash book is later dishonoured. The customer's account is
questions.explanation: Dishonour restores the customer's liability; therefore the customer's account is debited.

questions.text: Bank charges appearing only on the bank statement should initially be
options: credited to the bank column of the cash book
debited to the bank column of the cash book
questions.explanation: Bank charges reduce the bank balance, so the bank column is credited.

questions.text: A direct lodgement by a customer appears on the bank statement but not in the cash book. The cash book should be
questions.explanation: A direct lodgement increases the bank balance.

questions.text: Which item would normally require adjustment in the cash book before preparing a bank reconciliation statement
questions.explanation: Bank charges appearing on the bank statement but missing from the cash book must first be entered in the cash book.

questions.text: Opening inventory is ₦750,000, purchases are ₦3,600,000 and closing inventory is ₦900,000. Cost of sales is
If sales are ₦5,000,000 and cost of sales is ₦3,500,000, gross profit is
A business makes a markup of 25% on cost. If the cost is ₦800,000, selling price is
A trader sells goods for ₦1,200,000 at a markup of 20%. The cost is
questions.explanation: Selling price = 120% of cost. ₦1.2m ÷ 1.2 = ₦1m.

questions.text: A trader makes a margin of 30%. If sales are ₦2,000,000, cost of sales is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 30% × ₦2m = ₦600k. Cost = ₦2m − ₦600k = ₦1.4m.

questions.text: An increase in closing inventory, all other things being equal, will
questions.explanation: Closing inventory is deducted from cost of sales. A higher closing inventory reduces cost of sales and therefore increases gross profit.

questions.text: Opening inventory is understated by ₦80,000 while closing inventory is correctly stated. Gross profit is
questions.explanation: Understated opening inventory understates cost of sales, causing gross profit to be overstated by ₦80,000.

questions.text: Closing inventory is overstated by ₦100,000. The effect on gross profit is
questions.explanation: Closing inventory is deducted from cost of sales. Overstating it understates cost of sales and therefore overstates gross profit.

questions.text: Which of the following is excluded from the calculation of gross profit
questions.explanation: Office salaries are operating expenses, not direct trading costs.

questions.text: Which item is normally included in the trading account
questions.explanation: Carriage inward forms part of the cost of bringing goods into the business.

questions.text: Rent paid during the year was ₦720,000. Prepaid rent at the beginning was ₦40,000 and at the end was ₦70,000. Rent expense is
Insurance paid is ₦500,000. Opening prepaid insurance is ₦60,000 and closing prepaid insurance is ₦90,000. Insurance expense is
An expense accrued at year-end should be
options: deducted from the expense and shown as an asset
added to the expense and shown as a liability
questions.explanation: The expense belongs to the current period but remains unpaid, so it is added to expense and recognized as a liability.

questions.text: Income received in advance is treated as
questions.explanation: The business owes the service to the customer, making the amount a liability.

questions.text: A business receives ₦1,000,000 rent, of which ₦100,000 relates to next year. Current-year rent income is
A debtor owing ₦300,000 pays ₦285,000 in full settlement. Discount allowed is
A supplier grants a discount of ₦25,000 on a debt of ₦500,000. The amount paid is
A bad debt previously written off is later recovered. The amount recovered is treated as
questions.explanation: Recovery of a previously written-off debt is recognized as income.

questions.text: Trade receivables are ₦2,000,000. An allowance for doubtful debts of 4% is required. Net receivables are
questions.explanation: Allowance = 4% × ₦2m = ₦80k. Net receivables = ₦2m − ₦80k = ₦1,920,000.

questions.text: An existing allowance is ₦60,000 and the required allowance is ₦45,000. The reduction of ₦15,000 will
questions.explanation: Reducing the allowance reverses part of the previous expense and therefore increases profit.

questions.text: Current assets are ₦9,000,000 and current liabilities are ₦3,000,000. Current ratio is
Current assets are ₦7,500,000, inventory ₦2,500,000 and current liabilities ₦2,000,000. Acid-test ratio is
Sales are ₦8,000,000 and gross profit is ₦2,000,000. Gross profit margin is
Gross profit is ₦2,400,000 and operating expenses are ₦1,500,000. Net profit is
Net profit is ₦900,000 and sales are ₦6,000,000. Net profit margin is
Cost of sales is ₦4,800,000 and average inventory is ₦800,000. Inventory turnover is
Credit sales are ₦7,200,000 and average receivables are ₦1,200,000. Receivables turnover is
Using a 360-day year, a receivables turnover of 8 times gives an average collection period of
Credit purchases are ₦5,000,000 and average payables are ₦1,000,000. Payables turnover is
questions.explanation: ₦5m ÷ ₦1m = 5 times.

questions.text: A low receivables turnover ratio generally indicates
questions.explanation: A lower turnover means receivables are converted into cash less frequently.

questions.text: A and B share profits equally. The profit for the year is ₦1,800,000. A is entitled to a salary of ₦300,000 before sharing the residual profit. A's total share is
Partners A and B share profits 3:2. If A receives ₦900,000 as his share, total profit is

questions.explanation: Goodwill is an intangible non-current asset.

questions.text: When a new partner brings cash as his share of goodwill, the amount is generally credited to
options: cash and credited to old partners' capital/current accounts
questions.explanation: Cash increases, while the goodwill contribution is credited to the partners entitled to it.

options: It must have exactly two partners
Partners may contribute capital and share profits according to agreement
The business must be owned by government
questions.explanation: Partnership arrangements are based on agreement among the partners concerning contributions, responsibilities and profit sharing.

Preference shareholders generally have
options: priority over ordinary shareholders regarding dividends
no claim to dividends under any circumstances
unlimited voting rights in all matters
questions.explanation: Preference shares generally carry preferential rights to dividends and/or return of capital.

questions.text: Debenture holders are classified as
questions.explanation: Debenture holders lend funds to the company and are therefore creditors.

questions.text: Interest payable on debentures is
questions.explanation: Debenture interest is an expense incurred for borrowed funds.

questions.text: The authorized share capital of a company refers to
options: maximum share capital the company is permitted to issue under its constitution
questions.explanation: It represents the maximum share capital the company is authorized to issue.

questions.text: A non-profit organization receives subscriptions of ₦900,000. Opening arrears are ₦60,000 and closing arrears are ₦90,000. There are no subscriptions in advance. Subscription income is
The excess of income over expenditure in a non-profit organization is called
questions.explanation: Non-profit organizations refer to the excess of income over expenditure as a surplus.

questions.text: The accumulated fund of a non-profit organization is broadly equivalent to
questions.explanation: The accumulated fund represents the organization's net assets/equity.

questions.text: A receipts and payments account includes
options: all cash and bank receipts and payments
questions.explanation: It records all cash and bank movements regardless of whether they are capital or revenue.

questions.text: Which of the following would NOT normally appear in a receipts and payments account
questions.explanation: Depreciation is a non-cash expense.

questions.text: Opening capital is ₦4,500,000, closing capital ₦5,200,000, drawings ₦600,000 and additional capital ₦300,000. Profit is

questions.text: The purchases ledger control account is mainly used to
options: determine total amount owed to suppliers
determine total amount owed by customers
questions.explanation: It summarizes the balances and transactions relating to trade payables.

questions.text: The sales ledger control account helps determine

questions.text: A customer returns goods worth ₦40,000. In the sales ledger control account, this is
questions.explanation: Returns inward reduce the amount receivable from customers, so they are credited.

questions.text: Goods returned to a supplier are recorded in the purchases ledger control account as
questions.explanation: Returns outward reduce the amount owed to suppliers, so the control account is credited.

questions.text: Which document is normally issued by a seller to correct an overcharge to a customer
questions.explanation: A credit note reduces the customer's amount payable.

questions.text: A debit note is commonly used by a buyer to
options: inform the seller of goods returned
questions.explanation: A debit note can notify the supplier of returns or other amounts to be debited to the supplier's account.

questions.text: Which document provides evidence that payment has been received
questions.explanation: A receipt acknowledges payment received.

questions.text: An invoice is primarily used to
options: provide details of goods sold or purchased on credit
questions.explanation: An invoice provides details of a credit transaction, including quantities, prices and terms.

questions.text: A business's total assets are ₦12,000,000 and total liabilities are ₦4,500,000. Capital is

questions.text: A business purchases inventory for ₦700,000 cash and subsequently sells the inventory for ₦900,000 cash. The combined effect on cash is
questions.explanation: Cash decreases ₦700k and later increases ₦900k, giving a net increase of ₦200k.

questions.text: If sales are ₦9,000,000 and gross profit margin is 20%, cost of sales is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = ₦1.8m. Cost of sales = ₦9m − ₦1.8m = ₦7.2m.

questions.text: A trader's cost of sales is ₦6,000,000 and markup is 25%. Sales are

Which of the following would improve a company's working capital position, all else equal
options: Paying a current liability with cash
Converting a current liability into long-term debt
questions.explanation: Converting a current liability to a long-term liability reduces current liabilities without reducing current assets.

questions.text: A company's current ratio is 1:1. It purchases inventory on credit. The current ratio will generally
questions.explanation: Both current assets and current liabilities increase by the same amount. When the starting ratio is exactly 1:1, the ratio remains 1:1.

questions.text: Which of the following is a limitation of accounting information
options: It cannot capture every qualitative factor affecting a business
questions.explanation: Accounting focuses heavily on measurable financial information and may not fully capture qualitative factors such as employee morale or customer loyalty.

questions.text: The primary purpose of preparing financial statements is to
options: provide useful financial information to users
questions.explanation: Financial statements provide information useful to owners, management, investors, creditors and other users.

questions.text: A business has profit before depreciation of ₦2,400,000. Depreciation is ₦300,000. During the year, receivables increased by ₦250,000 and payables increased by ₦150,000. Using the indirect approach, cash generated from operations before other adjustments is
questions.explanation: Profit before depreciation = ₦2,400,000. Add depreciation = +₦300,000. Less increase in receivables = −₦250,000. Add increase in payables = +₦150,000. = ₦2,600,000.

questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes bookkeeping from accounting
options: Bookkeeping interprets information while accounting records transactions
Bookkeeping records financial transactions while accounting includes recording, classifying, summarizing and interpreting them
Bookkeeping is concerned only with assets while accounting is concerned only with liabilities
There is no distinction between the two
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping is mainly concerned with systematic recording of transactions, while accounting goes further to classify, summarize, interpret and communicate financial information.

questions.text: A business bought office equipment for ₦850,000 by cheque. What is the immediate effect on the accounting equation
options: Assets increase by ₦850,000 and capital decreases by ₦850,000
One asset increases by ₦850,000 while another asset decreases by ₦850,000
Assets increase and liabilities increase by ₦850,000
questions.explanation: Equipment increases by ₦850,000 while bank decreases by the same amount. Total assets therefore remain unchanged.

questions.text: Which accounting concept justifies treating the owner and the business as separate entities
questions.explanation: The business entity concept requires the transactions of the owner to be distinguished from those of the business.

questions.text: A proprietor takes goods costing ₦75,000 from the business for personal use. The correct treatment is to
questions.explanation: Goods withdrawn for personal use reduce purchases/inventory and are treated as drawings.

questions.text: Which of the following is most relevant to the concept of consistency
options: Using the same accounting method from one period to another unless there is a valid reason for changing it
Recording assets at their selling prices
questions.explanation: Consistency enables meaningful comparison between accounting periods.

questions.text: A company purchases goods on credit from Musa. Which source document would normally provide evidence of the transaction
questions.explanation: An invoice records details of goods supplied on credit.

questions.text: Which book of original entry is used primarily to record credit purchases of goods for resale
questions.explanation: Credit purchases of goods for resale are first recorded in the purchases journal.

questions.text: A business purchased goods worth ₦1,500,000 subject to a 12% trade discount. What amount should be recorded as purchases
A cheque received from a customer is dishonoured. The immediate effect is to
questions.explanation: Since the cheque failed, the amount is again owed by the customer.

questions.text: Which of the following errors will NOT cause the trial balance to disagree
options: Posting a transaction to the debit side only
Omitting the credit entry of a transaction
questions.explanation: An error of original entry affecting both sides equally will not disturb the equality of the trial balance.

questions.text: A suspense account is opened mainly because
options: the business has made a loss
the trial balance does not agree and the cause of the difference has not yet been identified
questions.explanation: Suspense accounts temporarily hold unexplained differences until errors are identified and corrected.

questions.text: Which error would normally be disclosed by a trial balance
options: Posting a debit without its corresponding credit
questions.explanation: A missing double-entry causes the debit and credit totals to differ.

questions.text: A three-column cash book contains
questions.explanation: The three-column cash book has cash, bank and discount columns.

questions.text: A cash discount allowed to a customer is recorded
options: on the debit side of the discount column
on the credit side of the discount column
questions.explanation: Discount allowed is an expense/loss to the business and is recorded on the debit side.

questions.text: The imprest system of petty cash is designed mainly to
options: eliminate the need for a cash book
maintain a fixed petty cash float
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, the petty cashier is periodically reimbursed to restore the float to its fixed amount.

questions.text: A petty cashier receives an imprest of ₦100,000 and spends ₦72,500 during the period. The reimbursement should be
questions.explanation: Reimbursement equals the amount actually spent: ₦72,500.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital expenditure
options: Purchase of a new delivery truck
questions.explanation: The purchase creates a non-current asset expected to provide benefits over several accounting periods.

questions.text: A machine cost ₦4,000,000 and has a residual value of ₦400,000. If its useful life is 8 years, annual straight-line depreciation is
An asset costing ₦2,500,000 is depreciated at 20% reducing balance. Its carrying amount after two years is
Which of the following would increase profit if all other factors remain constant
options: Reduction in provision for doubtful debts
questions.explanation: A reduction in the provision reverses part of the previous expense, increasing profit.

questions.text: Opening inventory is ₦1,200,000, purchases are ₦5,800,000 and closing inventory is ₦1,500,000. Cost of sales is

A trader sells goods at a markup of 25%. If the selling price is ₦1,500,000, the cost is

questions.explanation: Gross profit = 20% × ₦2.5m = ₦500,000. Cost of sales = ₦2,000,000.

questions.text: An increase in closing inventory, without any other change, will
questions.explanation: Closing inventory is deducted when calculating cost of sales.

questions.text: A business paid rent of ₦900,000. Opening prepaid rent was ₦80,000 and closing prepaid rent was ₦120,000. Rent expense is
Salaries paid during the year were ₦1,800,000. Salaries accrued at the beginning were ₦150,000 and accrued at the end were ₦220,000. Salaries expense is
If income is received in advance, it is
options: deducted from current income and treated as a liability
questions.explanation: The amount relates to a future period and represents an obligation to provide goods/services.

questions.text: Trade receivables are ₦3,000,000. A 5% allowance for doubtful debts is required. The net receivables are
questions.explanation: Allowance = 5% × ₦3m = ₦150,000. Net receivables = ₦2.85m.

questions.text: An existing allowance for doubtful debts is ₦90,000 while the new required allowance is ₦120,000. The adjustment will
questions.explanation: The provision increases by ₦30,000, creating an additional expense.

questions.text: A bank statement shows a credit balance of ₦1,250,000. Unpresented cheques amount to ₦180,000 while uncredited lodgements amount to ₦95,000. The cash-book balance is
questions.explanation: Cash-book balance = bank statement balance − unpresented cheques + uncredited lodgements = ₦1.25m − ₦180k + ₦95k = ₦1.165m.

questions.text: Which item is entered in the adjusted cash book when discovered during bank reconciliation
options: Bank charges omitted from the cash book
Cheque issued but not yet presented
questions.explanation: Bank charges appearing on the statement but absent from the cash book must be entered in the cash book.

questions.text: A standing order paid by the bank but not entered in the cash book should be
questions.explanation: The standing order reduces the bank balance, so the bank column is credited.

questions.text: A direct credit from a customer appears on the bank statement but is absent from the cash book. The cash book should be
questions.explanation: The direct credit increases the bank balance.

questions.text: Under FIFO, when prices are rising, closing inventory is generally valued at
questions.explanation: FIFO assumes the oldest units are issued first, leaving the more recent purchases in closing inventory.

options: check the arithmetical accuracy of individual sales ledger accounts
questions.explanation: The control account summarizes sales ledger transactions and helps check the individual accounts.

questions.text: Which of the following normally has a credit balance in the sales ledger control account
questions.explanation: Credit sales increase the amount owed by customers and are therefore credited in the control account.

questions.text: Which item is normally debited to the purchases ledger control account
questions.explanation: Cash paid reduces the amount owed to suppliers, so it is debited.

questions.text: A business has opening capital of ₦4,000,000, additional capital of ₦500,000, drawings of ₦700,000 and closing capital of ₦4,600,000. Profit is
questions.explanation: Closing capital = Opening capital + Additional capital + Profit − Drawings. ₦4.6m = ₦4m + ₦500k + Profit − ₦700k. Profit = ₦800,000.

questions.text: A sole trader has assets of ₦8,500,000 and liabilities of ₦2,700,000. His capital is
questions.explanation: Capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₦8.5m − ₦2.7m = ₦5.8m.

questions.text: Production overhead is ₦900,000 and prime cost is ₦3,800,000. Production cost is
questions.explanation: Production cost = Prime cost + Production overhead = ₦4.7m.

questions.text: Which of the following is a direct cost in manufacturing
questions.explanation: Direct materials can be directly traced to the product being manufactured.

questions.text: A non-profit organization receives subscriptions of ₦1,200,000. Opening arrears are ₦100,000, closing arrears ₦150,000, opening advance ₦60,000 and closing advance ₦80,000. Subscription income is
questions.explanation: Income = Cash received + closing arrears − opening arrears + opening advance − closing advance = ₦1.2m + ₦150k − ₦100k + ₦60k − ₦80k = ₦1.23m.

questions.text: The excess of expenditure over income in a non-profit organization is called
questions.explanation: A non-profit organization records an excess of expenditure over income as a deficit.

questions.text: Which of the following is normally excluded from an income and expenditure account
questions.explanation: Purchase of a building is a capital expenditure and is not an income-and-expenditure item.

questions.text: A partnership agreement provides that profits are shared A:B:C = 3:2:1. If divisible profit is ₦1,800,000, B's share is
questions.explanation: Total ratio = 6. B's share = 2/6 × ₦1.8m = ₦600,000.

questions.text: Partners A and B share profits 3:2. A is entitled to a salary of ₦400,000 before sharing a residual profit of ₦1,500,000. A's total entitlement is
questions.explanation: A receives 3/5 × ₦1.5m = ₦900k. Add salary ₦400k = ₦1.3m.

questions.text: When a new partner is admitted and goodwill is recognized, the goodwill attributable to old partners is normally shared according to their
questions.explanation: Existing partners are compensated for the goodwill they built up according to their old profit-sharing ratio, unless the agreement specifies otherwise.

questions.text: On dissolution of a partnership, the realization account is prepared primarily to determine
options: profit or loss on realization of assets and settlement of liabilities
questions.explanation: The realization account records disposal of assets and settlement of liabilities to determine the realization profit or loss.

questions.explanation: Discount = 5% × ₦5m = ₦250,000. Cash received = ₦4.75m.

questions.text: Which of the following is generally a capital reserve
questions.explanation: Share premium arises from the issue of shares above their nominal value and is classified as a capital reserve.

questions.text: A joint venture differs from a partnership mainly because a joint venture
options: is usually formed for a specific temporary business undertaking
questions.explanation: A joint venture is normally established for a particular project or transaction and ends when that undertaking is completed.

questions.text: Two venturers share joint venture profit in the ratio 3:2. If the profit is ₦750,000, the first venturer's share is
A branch sends goods costing ₦600,000 to head office. If the branch has not yet received the goods at year-end, the item represents
questions.explanation: Goods dispatched but not yet received by the destination are goods in transit.

questions.text: A branch receives goods from head office at invoice price rather than cost. The difference between invoice price and cost is generally known as
questions.explanation: The excess of invoice price over cost is called loading.

questions.text: The principal purpose of departmental accounts is to
options: determine the performance of individual departments
questions.explanation: Departmental accounts enable management to determine the profitability and performance of separate departments.

questions.text: A common expense shared by departments should ideally be apportioned according to
options: an appropriate basis related to the nature of the expense
questions.explanation: Expenses should be allocated using a logical basis—for example, floor area for rent or number of employees for certain staff costs.

questions.text: Under incomplete records, opening capital is ₦3,500,000 and closing capital is ₦4,300,000. Drawings during the year were ₦600,000 and additional capital was ₦200,000. Profit is
questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦4.3m + ₦600k − ₦200k − ₦3.5m = ₦1.2m.

questions.text: A statement of affairs is particularly useful under incomplete records for determining
options: capital by comparing assets and liabilities
questions.explanation: Capital is determined as total assets less total liabilities.

questions.text: If opening capital is ₦2,000,000 and closing capital is ₦2,800,000, with drawings of ₦500,000 and additional capital of ₦300,000, profit is
Which of the following is a source of government revenue
questions.explanation: Company income tax is a government revenue source.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital expenditure of government
options: Construction of a new public hospital
questions.explanation: Construction of a hospital creates a long-term public asset.

questions.text: Recurrent expenditure refers mainly to expenditure
options: incurred regularly in running government operations
questions.explanation: Salaries, utilities and routine administration are examples of recurrent expenditure.

questions.text: The Accountant-General of a government is primarily concerned with
options: maintaining government accounting records and preparing financial statements
questions.explanation: The Accountant-General is responsible for central government accounting and financial reporting functions.

questions.text: The Auditor-General's principal responsibility is to
questions.explanation: The Auditor-General provides independent audit oversight of public accounts.

questions.text: A warrant in government accounting primarily provides
questions.explanation: A warrant authorizes expenditure from an approved government appropriation.

questions.text: Virement in public sector accounting refers to
options: transfer of funds between approved budgetary heads subject to authorization
transfer of ownership of a company
questions.explanation: Virement involves authorized movement of funds from one budget provision to another.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major difference between cash and accrual accounting
options: Cash accounting recognizes transactions when cash changes hands, while accrual accounting recognizes them when income is earned or expenses are incurred
Cash accounting records assets while accrual accounting records liabilities only
questions.explanation: The key distinction is the timing of recognition.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an intangible asset
questions.explanation: A patent has identifiable economic value but no physical substance.

questions.text: Which qualitative characteristic makes accounting information useful for comparing the performance of different periods
questions.explanation: Comparability enables users to identify similarities and differences across periods or entities.

questions.text: Which branch of accounting is primarily concerned with determining and controlling the cost of production
questions.explanation: Cost accounting determines, analyzes and controls costs.

questions.text: The primary purpose of auditing is to
options: provide independent assurance on financial statements
questions.explanation: Auditing involves independent examination and expression of an opinion/assurance concerning financial information.

questions.text: Which of the following best demonstrates professional integrity by an accountant
options: Presenting financial information honestly and objectively
questions.explanation: Integrity requires honesty and straightforwardness in professional conduct.

questions.text: A computerized accounting system has an advantage over a manual system because it can
options: eliminate the need for accounting principles
process large volumes of transactions rapidly and consistently
guarantee that every input is correct
questions.explanation: Computerized systems improve speed and consistency, although incorrect input can still produce incorrect output.

questions.text: The accounting process in which raw transaction data is converted into useful reports is commonly described as
questions.explanation: Accounting information systems process transaction data into useful financial information.

questions.text: A major risk associated with computerized accounting is
questions.explanation: Cybersecurity and unauthorized access are important risks in computerized systems.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to improve internal control in a computerized accounting environment
options: Allowing one employee to authorize, record and reconcile every transaction
Using access controls and segregation of duties
questions.explanation: Access controls and segregation of duties reduce opportunities for unauthorized transactions and fraud.

questions.text: A manufacturing company has direct materials of ₦3,000,000, direct labour of ₦2,000,000 and direct expenses of ₦500,000. Factory overhead is ₦1,500,000. Production cost is
questions.explanation: Prime cost = ₦3m + ₦2m + ₦500k = ₦5.5m. Production cost = ₦5.5m + ₦1.5m = ₦7m.

questions.text: A customer owing ₦500,000 is allowed a discount of 4% for immediate settlement. The amount received is
questions.explanation: Discount = 4% × ₦500k = ₦20k. Cash received = ₦480k.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦7,500,000 and a gross margin of 28%. Its cost of sales is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 28% × ₦7.5m = ₦2.1m. Cost of sales = ₦7.5m − ₦2.1m = ₦5.4m.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦10,000,000, cost of sales of ₦6,000,000, administrative expenses of ₦1,200,000, selling expenses of ₦800,000 and finance cost of ₦200,000. What is the profit for the period
questions.explanation: Gross profit = ₦10m − ₦6m = ₦4m. Total expenses = ₦1.2m + ₦800k + ₦200k = ₦2.2m. Profit = ₦4m − ₦2.2m = ₦1.8m.

questions.text: A trader purchased goods for ₦800,000. He was allowed a trade discount of 10% and subsequently paid the supplier within the period allowed for a cash discount of 5%. What amount will be recorded as the cost of the goods
questions.explanation: Trade discount = 10% of ₦800,000 = ₦80,000. Cost recorded = ₦800,000 − ₦80,000 = ₦720,000. Cash discount is not deducted from the cost of purchases; it is treated separately when payment is made.

questions.text: A business commenced operations with cash of ₦2,500,000. It purchased equipment for ₦600,000 cash and goods on credit for ₦900,000. What is the proprietor's capital immediately after these transactions
questions.explanation: Capital introduced remains ₦2.5m. The equipment and cash purchase merely change the composition of assets, while the credit purchase creates a liability.

questions.text: Which of the following errors can occur without causing the trial balance to disagree

Posting an amount to the wrong side of an account
Recording a debit as ₦45,000 and the corresponding credit as ₦54,000
questions.explanation: If both entries are completely omitted, the debit and credit totals remain equal.

questions.text: A machine costing ₦5,000,000 is depreciated using the straight-line method at 10% per annum. If its residual value is estimated at ₦500,000, its annual depreciation is
A trader's opening inventory was ₦1,400,000. Purchases were ₦6,800,000 and closing inventory was ₦1,900,000. If carriage inward was ₦300,000, the cost of sales is

questions.explanation: Gross profit = 25% × ₦9m = ₦2.25m. Cost of sales = ₦9m − ₦2.25m = ₦6.75m.

questions.text: The balance of a purchases ledger control account is normally
questions.explanation: The purchases ledger control account represents amounts owed to suppliers.

A bank statement contains a standing order of ₦45,000 which has not yet been entered in the cash book. The adjustment required in the cash book is to
questions.explanation: A standing order is a payment from the bank account, so it reduces the bank balance.

questions.text: A petty cashier receives an imprest of ₦150,000. During the period, vouchers total ₦113,600. How much should be reimbursed
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, reimbursement equals the amount spent.

questions.text: Which of the following is not normally a book of original entry
questions.explanation: The ledger contains classified accounts into which entries from books of original entry are posted.

questions.explanation: The dishonoured cheque means the debtor once again owes the business the amount.

questions.text: A trader has assets of ₦12,800,000 and liabilities of ₦4,600,000. During the year, he introduces an additional ₦1,000,000 capital and makes drawings of ₦700,000. If the closing capital is ₦8,200,000, his profit is
questions.explanation: Opening capital = ₦12.8m − ₦4.6m = ₦8.2m. Closing capital = ₦8.2m. Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦8.2m + ₦700k − ₦1m − ₦8.2m = ₦700,000.

questions.text: A trader discovers that an amount of ₦75,000 received from a customer was credited to the customer's account but was also credited to sales account. This error is
questions.explanation: The receipt should be credited to the customer's account and debited to cash/bank. Treating it as sales involves using an inappropriate account classification.

questions.text: The main purpose of a suspense account is to
options: temporarily accommodate an unexplained difference in the trial balance
questions.explanation: A suspense account is temporary and is cleared once the errors causing the difference are identified.

questions.text: A company has current assets of ₦7,500,000, including inventory of ₦2,500,000. Current liabilities are ₦2,000,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦7.5m − ₦2.5m = ₦5m. Acid-test ratio = ₦5m ÷ ₦2m = 2.5:1.

questions.text: A business has cost of sales of ₦8,400,000 and average inventory of ₦1,400,000. The stock turnover is
questions.explanation: Stock turnover = Cost of sales ÷ Average inventory = ₦8.4m ÷ ₦1.4m = 6 times.

questions.text: Under FIFO, a business has 200 units @ ₦50 and 300 units @ ₦60. If 350 units are issued, the value of the issue is
Using the same information in the previous question, the value of closing inventory under FIFO is
questions.explanation: 150 units remain from the 300 units bought at ₦60. 150 × ₦60 = ₦9,000.

questions.text: A manufacturer incurs direct materials of ₦2,400,000, direct labour of ₦1,800,000, direct expenses of ₦300,000 and factory overhead of ₦900,000. The production cost is
questions.explanation: Prime cost = ₦2.4m + ₦1.8m + ₦300k = ₦4.5m. Production cost = ₦4.5m + ₦900k = ₦5.4m.

questions.text: Which of the following is most appropriately apportioned according to floor area occupied by departments
questions.explanation: Rent is commonly apportioned according to the floor area occupied by each department.

questions.text: A club receives subscriptions of ₦2,000,000 during the year. Subscriptions outstanding at the beginning and end are ₦150,000 and ₦220,000 respectively. Subscriptions received in advance at the beginning and end are ₦80,000 and ₦50,000 respectively. What is the subscription income for the year
questions.explanation: Income = Cash received + closing arrears − opening arrears + opening advance − closing advance = ₦2,000,000 + ₦220,000 − ₦150,000 + ₦80,000 − ₦50,000 = ₦2,100,000.

questions.text: Which of the following would normally appear in a receipts and payments account of a club
questions.explanation: Receipts and payments accounts record actual cash and bank receipts and payments during the period.

questions.text: Partners A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. Their divisible profit is ₦2,500,000. A receives a salary of ₦300,000 before the remaining profit is shared. What is A's total entitlement
questions.explanation: Residual profit = ₦2.5m − ₦300k = ₦2.2m. A's share = 3/5 × ₦2.2m = ₦1.32m. Total = ₦1.32m + ₦300k = ₦1.62m.

questions.text: A company issues 1,500,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each at ₦1.60 per share. The amount credited to the share premium account is
A company has 2,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each. It declares a dividend of 12%. The dividend payable is
A branch account is primarily prepared by head office to determine
options: the branch's gross and net performance
the depreciation of all company assets
questions.explanation: Branch accounting enables head office to determine the financial performance of the branch.

questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦4.2m + ₦500k − ₦300k − ₦3m = ₦1.4m.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital expenditure by government
questions.explanation: Construction of a highway creates a long-term public asset.

questions.text: Which government officer is primarily responsible for the independent audit of public accounts
questions.explanation: The Auditor-General independently audits public accounts and reports on them.

questions.text: Virement in government accounting refers to
options: transferring funds between approved budgetary provisions subject to authorization
transferring government assets to private individuals
questions.explanation: Virement allows an authorized transfer of funds between budgetary provisions.

questions.text: Which of the following is an advantage of a computerized accounting system
options: It allows rapid processing and retrieval of accounting information
It removes the need for internal controls
questions.explanation: Computerized systems can process, store and retrieve large amounts of accounting information efficiently. They do not eliminate errors or the need for controls.

questions.text: A trader has current assets of ₦9,600,000 and current liabilities of ₦3,200,000. He pays ₦800,000 to a creditor using cash. What is the new current ratio
questions.explanation: New current assets = ₦9.6m − ₦800k = ₦8.8m. New current liabilities = ₦3.2m − ₦800k = ₦2.4m. Ratio = ₦8.8m ÷ ₦2.4m = 3.67:1.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦12,000,000 and cost of sales of ₦7,200,000. Operating expenses are ₦1,500,000. What is the operating profit
questions.explanation: Gross profit = ₦12m − ₦7.2m = ₦4.8m. Operating profit = ₦4.8m − ₦1.5m = ₦3.3m.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the prudence concept
options: Expected losses should be recognized when reasonably foreseeable, while unrealized gains should not be anticipated
Every transaction must be recorded only when cash is received
questions.explanation: Prudence requires caution in recognizing uncertain gains and losses so that financial statements are not overstated.

questions.text: A business purchases a motor vehicle for ₦6,000,000. It pays ₦2,000,000 immediately and agrees to pay the balance later. What is the immediate effect on the accounting equation
options: Assets increase ₦6m; liabilities increase ₦4m; capital decreases ₦2m
Assets increase ₦6m; liabilities increase ₦4m; capital is unchanged
questions.explanation: The vehicle increases assets by ₦6m. Cash decreases by ₦2m, while the ₦4m unpaid balance creates a liability. Net assets increase by ₦4m, but this is matched by the new liability, so capital is unchanged.

questions.text: A trader purchased goods with a list price of ₦800,000 and was allowed a trade discount of 10%. He later paid the supplier and received a cash discount of 5%. What amount should initially be recorded in the purchases account
questions.explanation: Trade discount = 10% × ₦800,000 = ₦80,000. Therefore, purchase cost = ₦800,000 − ₦80,000 = ₦720,000. Cash discount is dealt with when payment is made.

questions.text: A business has assets of ₦9,500,000 and liabilities of ₦3,200,000. The owner introduces an additional ₦600,000 capital and subsequently withdraws ₦400,000. What is the owner's capital immediately after these transactions
questions.explanation: Initial capital = ₦9.5m − ₦3.2m = ₦6.3m. New capital = ₦6.3m + ₦600k − ₦400k = ₦6.5m.

questions.text: A trader purchases goods costing ₦1,200,000 and sells them at a markup of 100%. If he subsequently allows customers a 20% trade discount on the marked selling price, the actual selling price is
questions.explanation: Marked price = ₦1.2m × 2 = ₦2.4m. Discount = 20% × ₦2.4m = ₦480k. Actual selling price = ₦1.92m.

questions.text: A customer owing ₦800,000 is allowed a cash discount of 6% for immediate settlement. The amount received is
questions.explanation: Discount = 6% × ₦800k = ₦48k. Amount received = ₦752k.

questions.text: A business pays ₦1,000,000 to a creditor and receives a cash discount of ₦200,000. What amount is credited to the bank account
questions.explanation: The business actually pays ₦1m − ₦200k = ₦800k.

questions.text: Which of the following errors will cause the trial balance to disagree
options: Posting a transaction to the wrong personal account but on the correct side
Entering ₦50,000 as a debit but ₦5,000 as the corresponding credit
questions.explanation: The debit and credit amounts differ by ₦45,000, causing the trial balance totals to disagree.

questions.text: A purchase of office furniture for ₦900,000 was debited to the purchases account. The error is
questions.explanation: Furniture is a non-current asset, not goods purchased for resale. The error is therefore one of principle.

questions.text: A transaction is completely omitted from the books. Which of the following statements is correct
options: Only the debit side of the trial balance is affected
The trial balance can still agree
A suspense account must automatically be opened
questions.explanation: Both the debit and credit entries are missing, so equality is maintained.

questions.text: A suspense account has a debit balance of ₦45,000. It is later discovered that a receipt of ₦25,000 from a customer was correctly entered in the cash book but credited to the customer's account as ₦2,500. What is the correcting entry to clear the suspense account
questions.explanation: The customer's account was credited with ₦2,500 instead of ₦25,000 — a short credit of ₦22,500. To correct this, the customer's account must be credited with ₦22,500, while suspense is debited with the same amount to clear the balance. The original debit balance of ₦45,000 is therefore cleared.

questions.text: A three-column cash book contains

questions.text: A petty cashier operates an imprest system of ₦100,000. During the week, expenses amounted to ₦73,500. What amount should be reimbursed
questions.explanation: Reimbursement restores the petty cash float to ₦100,000, so it equals the amount spent: ₦73,500.

questions.text: Which of the following is recorded on the credit side of the discount column of a three-column cash book
questions.explanation: Discount received is a gain to the business and is recorded on the credit side.

questions.text: A bank statement shows a balance of ₦1,500,000. Unpresented cheques total ₦240,000 while lodgements not yet credited by the bank amount to ₦160,000. The corresponding cash-book balance is
questions.explanation: Cash book = Bank statement − unpresented cheques + uncredited lodgements = ₦1.5m − ₦240k + ₦160k = ₦1.42m.

questions.explanation: Bank charges reduce the bank balance and therefore the bank column of the cash book is credited.

questions.explanation: A royalty based directly on units produced can be traced directly to the cost of production.

questions.text: A non-profit organization has subscriptions received during the year of ₦1,500,000. Subscriptions outstanding were ₦100,000 at the beginning and ₦160,000 at the end. Subscriptions received in advance were ₦50,000 at the beginning and ₦30,000 at the end. Subscription income is

questions.explanation: A surplus is the excess of income over expenditure in a non-profit organization.

questions.explanation: Residual profit = ₦1.5m − ₦200k = ₦1.3m. B receives 2/5 × ₦1.3m = ₦520,000.

questions.text: A partnership's goodwill is valued at ₦900,000. A new partner is admitted and the old partners A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. If the new partner brings his share of goodwill in cash and is entitled to 1/5 of future profits, the amount of goodwill he contributes is
questions.explanation: The new partner's share is 1/5. 1/5 × ₦900,000 = ₦180,000.

questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦3.6m + ₦400k − ₦300k − ₦2.5m = ₦1.2m.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital expenditure of government
questions.explanation: Construction of a hospital creates a long-term public asset and is therefore capital expenditure.

questions.text: The officer primarily responsible for keeping the financial records of the Federal Government and preparing its financial statements is the
questions.explanation: The Accountant-General is responsible for central government accounting and financial reporting functions.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important control in a computerized accounting system
options: Allowing unrestricted access to all accounting records
Segregating authorization, processing and review functions
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties reduces the risk of unauthorized transactions and fraud.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦8,000,000, opening inventory of ₦900,000, purchases of ₦4,500,000, closing inventory of ₦700,000 and operating expenses of ₦1,200,000. What is the operating profit
questions.explanation: Cost of sales = ₦900k + ₦4.5m − ₦700k = ₦4.7m. Gross profit = ₦8m − ₦4.7m = ₦3.3m. Operating profit = ₦3.3m − ₦1.2m = ₦2.1m.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦15,000,000, cost of sales of ₦9,000,000 and operating expenses of ₦2,500,000. What is the net profit margin
questions.explanation: Gross profit = ₦15m − ₦9m = ₦6m. Net profit = ₦6m − ₦2.5m = ₦3.5m. Net profit margin = ₦3.5m ÷ ₦15m × 100 = 23.33%.

questions.text: A machine costing ₦6,000,000 has a useful life of 8 years and a residual value of ₦600,000. Using the straight-line method, what is the net book value after 3 years
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (₦6m − ₦600k) ÷ 8 = ₦675,000. After 3 years, accumulated depreciation = ₦2.025m. NBV = ₦6m − ₦2.025m = ₦3.975m.

questions.text: A trader purchased goods worth ₦2,000,000 subject to a 15% trade discount and a further 5% cash discount for prompt payment. The amount recorded as purchases is
questions.explanation: Trade discount = 15% × ₦2m = ₦300,000. Net purchase = ₦2m − ₦300k = ₦1.7m. Cash discount is not deducted from purchases.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦6,500,000, current liabilities of ₦2,600,000, and inventory of ₦1,300,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦6.5m − ₦1.3m = ₦5.2m. Acid-test ratio = ₦5.2m ÷ ₦2.6m = 2.0:1.

questions.text: A company has issued 5,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦0.50 each. If the company declares a dividend of 8%, the dividend payable is
questions.explanation: Total nominal value = 5,000,000 × ₦0.50 = ₦2.5m. Dividend = 8% × ₦2.5m = ₦200,000.

questions.text: A manufacturing business has prime cost of ₦4,200,000 and factory overhead of ₦1,800,000. Opening work-in-progress was ₦500,000 and closing work-in-progress was ₦700,000. The cost of production is
questions.explanation: Production cost = Prime cost + Factory overhead + Opening WIP − Closing WIP = ₦4.2m + ₦1.8m + ₦500k − ₦700k = ₦5.8m.

questions.text: A partner withdraws goods costing ₦45,000 from the partnership for personal use. The accounting entry is
questions.explanation: Goods withdrawn by a partner are treated as drawings and reduce purchases/inventory.

questions.text: A club has subscriptions received in advance of ₦120,000 at the beginning of the year and ₦90,000 at the end. Subscriptions outstanding were ₦80,000 at the beginning and ₦110,000 at the end. If cash received during the year was ₦2,500,000, the subscription income is
questions.explanation: Income = Cash received + closing arrears − opening arrears + opening advance − closing advance = ₦2.5m + ₦110k − ₦80k + ₦120k − ₦90k = ₦2.56m.

questions.text: A business has opening capital of ₦5,000,000, closing capital of ₦6,200,000, drawings of ₦800,000 and additional capital of ₦400,000. The profit for the year is
questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦6.2m + ₦800k − ₦400k − ₦5m = ₦1.6m.

questions.text: A trader has sales of ₦8,500,000 and a gross profit margin of 32%. What is the cost of sales
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 32% × ₦8.5m = ₦2.72m. Cost of sales = ₦8.5m − ₦2.72m = ₦5.78m.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦10,000,000 and current liabilities of ₦4,000,000. It purchases inventory worth ₦1,000,000 on credit. The new current ratio is
questions.explanation: New current assets = ₦11m. New current liabilities = ₦5m. Ratio = ₦11m ÷ ₦5m = 2.2:1.

questions.text: A business has credit sales of ₦10,000,000. Opening receivables were ₦1,200,000 and closing receivables were ₦1,800,000. The receivables turnover is
questions.explanation: Average receivables = (₦1.2m + ₦1.8m) ÷ 2 = ₦1.5m. Receivables turnover = ₦10m ÷ ₦1.5m = 6.67 times.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of revenue expenditure
options: Cost of rebuilding a damaged warehouse
Repairs and maintenance of office equipment
Purchase of a new delivery vehicle
questions.explanation: Repairs and maintenance are revenue expenditure as they maintain existing assets rather than improving them.

questions.text: A partner is entitled to 10% interest on capital of ₦800,000. If the partnership makes a profit of ₦600,000 before interest, what is the interest on capital
questions.explanation: Interest = 10% × ₦800,000 = ₦80,000. This is an appropriation of profit, not an expense.

questions.text: A company issues debentures of ₦5,000,000 at a discount of 8%. The amount received is
questions.explanation: Discount = 8% × ₦5m = ₦400,000. Amount received = ₦5m − ₦400k = ₦4.6m.

questions.text: A trader's mark-up is 40% on cost. If the selling price is ₦2,800,000, what is the cost
questions.explanation: Selling price = 140% of cost. Cost = ₦2.8m ÷ 1.40 = ₦2m.

questions.text: A business has cost of sales of ₦6,400,000. If the gross profit margin is 20%, what are the sales
questions.explanation: If gross profit margin is 20%, then cost of sales is 80% of sales. Sales = ₦6.4m ÷ 0.80 = ₦8m.

questions.text: A partnership has assets of ₦7,800,000 and liabilities of ₦2,200,000. If partners' capital accounts show ₦4,000,000, what is the balance on the current accounts
questions.explanation: Total capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₦7.8m − ₦2.2m = ₦5.6m. Current account balances = ₦5.6m − ₦4m = ₦1.6m.

questions.text: A non-profit organization has an accumulated fund of ₦3,200,000 at the beginning of the year. During the year, income was ₦900,000 and expenditure was ₦750,000. What is the closing accumulated fund
questions.explanation: Surplus = ₦900k − ₦750k = ₦150k. Closing accumulated fund = ₦3.2m + ₦150k = ₦3.35m.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦12,000,000 and a gross profit margin of 40%. Operating expenses are ₦2,400,000. What is the operating profit
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 40% × ₦12m = ₦4.8m. Operating profit = ₦4.8m − ₦2.4m = ₦2.4m.

questions.text: A company issues 1,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each at ₦1.20. What is the total amount received
questions.explanation: Total received = ₦1.20 × 1,000,000 = ₦1.2m. Of this, ₦1m is share capital and ₦200k is share premium.

questions.text: A trader's gross profit is ₦3,600,000. If the gross profit margin is 30%, the sales are
questions.explanation: Sales = Gross profit ÷ Margin = ₦3.6m ÷ 0.30 = ₦12m.

questions.text: A business has current ratio of 2.5:1 and current liabilities of ₦3,000,000. What is the value of current assets
questions.explanation: Current assets = Current ratio × Current liabilities = 2.5 × ₦3m = ₦7.5m.

questions.text: A partnership has a profit of ₦2,000,000. Partners A and B share profits in the ratio 2:3. A is entitled to a salary of ₦300,000. What is B's total share
