questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦7,200,000, inventory of ₦2,400,000 and current liabilities of ₦2,400,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦7.2m − ₦2.4m = ₦4.8m. Acid-test ratio = ₦4.8m ÷ ₦2.4m = 2:1.

questions.text: A business has cost of sales of ₦12,000,000 and average inventory of ₦2,000,000. The stock turnover is
questions.explanation: Stock turnover = ₦12m ÷ ₦2m = 6 times.

questions.text: A company has 5,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦0.50 each. If the company declares a dividend of 8%, the dividend payable is
questions.explanation: Total nominal value = 5m × ₦0.50 = ₦2.5m. Dividend = 8% × ₦2.5m = ₦200,000.

questions.text: A manufacturing business has prime cost of ₦6,000,000 and factory overhead of ₦2,000,000. Opening work-in-progress was ₦500,000 and closing WIP was ₦700,000. The production cost is
questions.explanation: Production cost = Prime cost + Factory overhead + Opening WIP − Closing WIP = ₦6m + ₦2m + ₦500k − ₦700k = ₦7.8m.

questions.text: A business has credit sales of ₦24,000,000. Opening receivables were ₦3,000,000 and closing receivables were ₦4,000,000. The receivables turnover is
questions.explanation: Average receivables = (₦3m + ₦4m) ÷ 2 = ₦3.5m. Receivables turnover = ₦24m ÷ ₦3.5m = 6.86 times.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦18,000,000 and a gross profit margin of 35%. What is the gross profit
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 35% × ₦18m = ₦6.3m.

questions.text: A company has issued share capital of ₦12,000,000. If the company repurchases ₦3,000,000 worth of shares, the issued share capital becomes
questions.explanation: Issued share capital = ₦12m − ₦3m = ₦9m.

questions.text: A partner is entitled to 10% interest on capital of ₦2,000,000. The interest on capital is

A non-profit organization has subscriptions received in advance of ₦200,000 at the beginning and ₦150,000 at the end. Subscriptions outstanding were ₦180,000 at the beginning and ₦250,000 at the end. If cash received is ₦4,000,000, the subscription income is
questions.explanation: Income = Cash + closing arrears − opening arrears + opening advance − closing advance = ₦4m + ₦250k − ₦180k + ₦200k − ₦150k = ₦4.12m.

questions.text: A club has an accumulated fund of ₦2,000,000. During the year, the club had income of ₦1,200,000 and expenditure of ₦1,400,000. The closing accumulated fund is
questions.explanation: Deficit = ₦1.4m − ₦1.2m = ₦200k. Closing accumulated fund = ₦2m − ₦200k = ₦1.8m.

questions.text: A company issues 3,000,000 ordinary shares at ₦2.50 each. The nominal value is ₦1.50. The total amount credited to share premium is
questions.explanation: Premium per share = ₦2.50 − ₦1.50 = ₦1.00. Total premium = ₦1.00 × 3,000,000 = ₦3m.

questions.text: A manufacturing business has direct materials of ₦5,000,000, direct labour of ₦3,000,000 and factory overhead of ₦2,000,000. The prime cost is
questions.explanation: Prime cost = Direct materials + Direct labour = ₦5m + ₦3m = ₦8m.

questions.text: A trader's mark-up is 25% on cost. If the selling price is ₦5,000,000, the cost is
questions.explanation: Selling price = 125% of cost. Cost = ₦5m ÷ 1.25 = ₦4m.

questions.text: A business has cost of sales of ₦8,400,000 and a gross profit margin of 30%. The sales are
questions.explanation: If margin is 30%, cost is 70% of sales. Sales = ₦8.4m ÷ 0.70 = ₦12m.

questions.text: A business has a current ratio of 2.2:1 and current liabilities of ₦5,000,000. The current assets are
questions.explanation: Current assets = 2.2 × ₦5m = ₦11m.

questions.text: A non-current asset costing ₦8,000,000 has accumulated depreciation of ₦3,200,000. If it is sold for ₦4,200,000, the result is
questions.explanation: Net book value = ₦8m − ₦3.2m = ₦4.8m. Loss on sale = ₦4.8m − ₦4.2m = ₦600,000.

questions.text: A trader's gross profit is ₦5,400,000. If the gross profit margin is 45%, the sales are
questions.explanation: Sales = Gross profit ÷ Margin = ₦5.4m ÷ 0.45 = ₦12m.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦14,000,000, inventory of ₦4,000,000 and current liabilities of ₦5,000,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦14m − ₦4m = ₦10m. Acid-test ratio = ₦10m ÷ ₦5m = 2:1.

questions.text: The accounting concept that requires that financial statements should not be misleading is the
questions.explanation: The fair presentation concept requires that financial statements present information honestly and without misleading users.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦20,000,000 and a gross profit margin of 30%. If operating expenses are ₦3,000,000, the operating profit is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 30% × ₦20m = ₦6m. Operating profit = ₦6m − ₦3m = ₦3m.

questions.text: A company issues 4,000,000 ordinary shares at ₦3.00 each. The nominal value is ₦2.00. The total amount received is
questions.explanation: Total received = 4,000,000 × ₦3.00 = ₦12m.

questions.text: A business has assets of ₦30,000,000 and liabilities of ₦11,500,000. If the owner withdraws ₦800,000 and introduces ₦1,200,000, what is the new capital
questions.explanation: Initial capital = ₦30m − ₦11.5m = ₦18.5m. New capital = ₦18.5m − ₦800k + ₦1.2m = ₦18.9m.

questions.text: The accounting principle that requires that expenses should be recognized in the same period as the revenue they helped to generate is the
questions.explanation: The matching concept requires that expenses be matched with the revenue they generate in the same accounting period to determine accurate profit.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦8,400,000 and current liabilities of ₦2,800,000. It purchases inventory worth ₦1,200,000 on credit. What is the new current ratio
questions.explanation: New current assets = ₦8.4m + ₦1.2m = ₦9.6m. New current liabilities = ₦2.8m + ₦1.2m = ₦4.0m. New current ratio = ₦9.6m ÷ ₦4.0m = 2.4:1.

questions.text: The accounting concept that assumes a business will continue to operate indefinitely is the
questions.explanation: The going concern concept assumes that the business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future, justifying the use of historical cost for assets.

questions.text: A machine costing ₦12,000,000 has an estimated useful life of 8 years and a residual value of ₦1,200,000. Using the straight-line method, what is the accumulated depreciation after 5 years
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (₦12m − ₦1.2m) ÷ 8 = ₦10.8m ÷ 8 = ₦1.35m. Accumulated depreciation after 5 years = ₦1.35m × 5 = ₦6.75m.

questions.text: The accounting principle that requires that similar items should be treated in the same way from one period to the next is the
questions.explanation: The consistency concept requires that the same accounting methods and principles should be used from one accounting period to another to allow meaningful comparison of financial statements.

anticipated losses be provided for but anticipated profits not recognised

topic_questions.explanation: Drawings reduce cash and reduce the owner's capital.

topic_questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital − Opening capital + Drawings = ₦1,700,000.

topic_questions.explanation: Capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₦5,000,000 − ₦1,800,000 = ₦3,200,000.

topic_questions.text: Total assets are ₦7,500,000 and capital is ₦5,000,000. Liabilities are
topic_questions.explanation: Liabilities = Assets − Capital = ₦7,500,000 − ₦5,000,000 = ₦2,500,000.

topic_questions.explanation: Liabilities = Assets − Capital = ₦4,200,000 − ₦3,000,000 = ₦1,200,000.

topic_questions.text: The main purpose of accounting is to

topic_questions.explanation: Management works within the organisation; the others are external users.

topic_questions.text: Book-keeping is best described as
options: the systematic recording of business transactions
topic_questions.explanation: Book-keeping is the recording aspect, while accounting also classifies, summarises and interprets.

topic_questions.text: Opening capital was ₦2,000,000, closing capital ₦2,600,000 and drawings ₦300,000. If no further capital was introduced, the profit for the year was
topic_questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital − Opening capital + Drawings = ₦900,000.

topic_questions.explanation: Under the business entity concept, the business and its owner are separate; only business transactions are recorded in the business books.

topic_questions.text: The effect of the owner introducing cash into the business is that
topic_questions.explanation: Cash (an asset) rises and so does the owner's capital.

an expense paid in advance only
an amount owed by the business
topic_questions.explanation: Assets are resources controlled by the business from past events from which future economic benefits are expected.

must be approved by an auditor

topic_questions.text: A liability is
options: the owner's claim on the business
an obligation of the business to pay outsiders

topic_questions.text: A business has assets of ₦8,500,000 and liabilities of ₦3,200,000. Its capital is

will continue operating for the foreseeable future

prove that there are no errors at all
topic_questions.explanation: It checks that total debits equal total credits, but does not prove complete accuracy.

topic_questions.text: The ledger is known as the book of

debiting Discount allowed and crediting the customer

debiting Cash and crediting the debtor
debiting the debtor and crediting Bad debts

debit the customer, credit Sales returns
debit Sales returns, credit the customer's account

the wrong class of account is used
a wrong amount is used on both sides

credit purchases of goods for resale

debiting the supplier and crediting Discount received
